newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED V TOTTENHAM - MATCH ANALYSIS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MANCHESTER UNITED V TOTTENHAM - MATCH ANALYSIS.

text.p: Following is an analysis of the strengths and weaknesses of Manchester United and Tottenham who meet in the F.A. Cup third round at Old Trafford on Sunday (1600 GMT):

Playing style: A basic 4-3-3 style but in name only as manager Alex Ferguson changes his playing style to suit the occasion. Traditionally Manchester United play expansively, attacking down the flanks or coming through the middle with equal ease.

Strengths: Proven class in almost every position with players of great flair and vision like Eric Cantona, Ryan Giggs and David Beckham capable of turning a match in a flash. The driving force of Roy Keane, recently back in the side after injury, adds steel to an already tough framework.

Weaknesses: The volatile temperament of Roy Keane, and to a lesser extent these days, Cantona. Some inexperience among younger players has cost United matches, most notably recently against Fenerbahce and Juventus in the European Cahampions' League.

Motivation: Manchester United open the defence of the F.A. Cup which they won for a record ninth time in May against the club with whom they previously shared the joint record of eight wins. United are also attempting to become the first club to play in four successive F.A. Cup finals.

Playing style: Recently Tottenham manager Gerry Francis, a firm believer in an orthodox 4-4-2 style of play, has been experimenting with playing three across the back with fairly mixed results. Tottenham, like United, are traditionally one of the most exciting teams to watch in England, but under Francis their traditional flair has been sacrificed for a more pragmatic and often boringly nondescript approach.

Strengths: After being hammered 7-1 by Newcastle on Saturday and 6-1 by first division Bolton in the League Cup in November it is hard to pinpoint Tottenham's current strengths. Apart from those hammerings, the defence generally has a more organised look about it than it did under former manager Ossie Ardiles and new Norwegian signing Steffen Iversen obviously has vast potential. Defender Sol Campbell has been impressive.

Weaknesses: Lack of a creative midfielder is at the heart of Tottenham's problems. England striker Teddy Sheringham, playing in a deeper role this season has also flattered to decieve and looks past his best while injuries to Darren Anderton, Gary Mabbutt and Chris Armstrong have unsettled the side, which is clearly going through a period of considerable transition.

Motivation: If Spurs lose at Old Trafford on Sunday their season is effectively over. Already out of the championship race, and the League Cup, if they were to fail in the F.A. Cup, one competition in which they usually do well, many Spurs fans would call for Gerry Francis's head.
